title: Works Well But Surface Gets a Little Too Hot
text:
Works Well But Surface Gets a Little Too Hot. This is my first exposure to electric kettles, having used a whistling tea kettle for many years. While it seems to work very well and it does what it is supposed to do I found that some caution is required when using it due to surface and steam heat.

The idea of this type of kettle is very straightforward - it contains an integrated hot plate in the bottom of the kettle that heats up quickly and is used specifically for boiling water. Because of the low wattage it draws less electricity than using a stove top kettle or the microwave and because of the rapid heating it boils water very quickly which saves time.

I have used the kettle to heat a small amount of water and to heat the full kettle's worth and understandably it takes longer to heat more. This should not be a huge surprise. That said, it still works quickly and the water boils in a lot less time than when heated up in a microwave (which I find to be faster than the stove top). It does a great job of getting the water boiling quickly and without risking a spill.

In spite of its usefulness in saving time and energy, I have two reservations when it comes to using this kettle. My first observation is that the surface of the kettle's pitcher gets very hot, to the point of discomfort when you touch it. Well, of course it's going to get warm but the fact that it gets as warm as it does concerns me. It would have been nice if the pitcher was better insulated (or, rather, insulated at all). More unpleasant, though, is that after the water is hot if you open the top for pouring a cloud of steam tends to billow out and it's a little too easy to get a steam burn if caution is not used. Sure, you should not stick your hand in there and it should be obvious that there will be steam but the fact that it comes straight up and out is concerning.

This is not a bad kettle. It's actually a nice product and it works as advertised. Unfortunately, it needs a design revisit.

product_metadata.title: Bodum Bistro Large Electric Water Kettle, Red
features: It's the most energy efficient way to boil water
Save energy by boiling just the amount of water you need; boil anywhere from 8-Ounce to 51-Ounce at a time
Cordless carafe makes pouring easy anywhere
Available in two sizes (1.0 l, 1.5 l) and in black, orange, red, green, and white
description: Bringing water to a boil seems like the most basic of kitchen chores. And yet, it's really more complex than you might think. For example, is there a way to use less energy doing it? What's the quickest and also the safest way? The Bistro Water Kettle is the answer to all these questions. It's the most energy efficient way to boil water and there is no excess water boiled - just the amount that's really needed for your coffee or tea. It's super quick and safe as the boiling water is not exposed like it would be in a pan. The Bistro Water Kettle is made from plastic, stainless steel and silicone. It comes in two different sizes (1l and 1.5l) and in black, orange, red, green, and white.
